AccountLinkRequest.description: What the web app knows from the sign-in besides the signed identity: the display name.

image.description: The Google profile picture URL. Kept only when it is an https URL on lh3.googleusercontent.com; anything else is silently stored as null. Updated on every call, and cleared when absent.

AccountLinkRequest.title: AccountLinkRequest

AdminActionEvent.description:
A staff action that changed no appointment (a reminder sent now, "running late", an
invitation), for a viewer of the live feed: what happened and, for the two patient
notifications, the doctor and the visit time. No person, no reason, no address. Streamed only
by the Go gateway from ``staff_action_audit``; it never travels through the push service.
AdminActionEvent.title: AdminActionEvent

avatar_url.description: The patient's Google profile picture (https on lh3.googleusercontent.com), only for owners and admins; null for viewers, for patients who never signed in with Google or have no picture, and for every demo patient. Show initials when null.

AdminEvent.description: A booking changed, for the staff dashboard. No appointment or patient identifiers.

AttendanceRequest.description: The reason is optional for a first mark and required to change an earlier one.

cursor.description: "<txid>.<id>" read before the slots, in the same moment: every pushed event at or before it is already reflected in `slots`. Accept a newer response only if its cursor is not older than the one you hold.

taken.description: Starts of this day's grid that are booked (clinic-local offset, like `slots`): the times the doctor works that overlap a booking. Starts only; nothing says who holds them. A time is in `slots` or in `taken`, never both.

ChangeItem.description: One booking, reschedule or cancellation, placed by the day the change happened.

ClaimedReminder.description:

clinic the doctor works at (the email shows the time in that zone).

DoctorNoticeClaim.description:

sent, skipped, out of attempts or held by another sender, and there is nothing to do.

updated.description: False when the row was not held by a claim or was final.

retryable.description: Whether sending again can help now: a failed row with attempts left, or a pending row nothing is sending any more (never claimed after a grace period, or its claim ran out). A row that is pending with every attempt used is reported as failed.

UTC), and ``remaining``, how many more may be sent now, which is the smaller of the two.

EmailRelease.description: Which day and month a reserved email that was never sent is given back to.
EmailRelease.title: EmailRelease

EmailReservation.description:
The answer to "may I send one more email": ``granted`` means one was taken from both the day
and the month (give it back with ``/emails/release`` if the send then fails); otherwise
``reason`` names the cap that refused it. ``day`` and ``month`` are what it was taken from.

InviteCreated.description:
Returned once, on creation. ``token`` is the raw secret for the email link: it is not
stored (only its SHA-256 is), not logged and cannot be read again.

To email the invitation: when ``deliver`` is true, send the link ``/invite/<token>`` to
``email`` (Idempotency-Key ``invite/<id>``), then POST ``/internal/admin/audit/<audit_id>/
notified``. A reserved example address is "demo, not sent": ``deliver`` is false, the audit row
says so and nothing may be sent.

avatar_url.description: As on the appointment list: owners and admins only, else null.

MeAppointmentCreate.description: Booking as the signed-in patient: the patient comes from the account, never from the body.

NotifyItem.description:

sends the email (Idempotency-Key = `audit_id`) and then marks the audit row notified. For a
demo or address-less patient nothing is to be sent and `email` is null.

ReminderBatch.description: What one run may send now: the claimed appointments and the day's email budget.

ReminderRequest.description: Why the reminder goes now. Optional: it defaults to a standard line in the audit row.

minutes.description: How late the doctor expects to be.

local_date.description: Clinic-local date of the slot (the channel's date).

seq.description: "<txid>.<id>.<part>": apply a message only if it sorts after the last one applied and its (txid, id) is after the cursor of the availability response in use.

get.description: Activity series, totals and per-doctor load for the clinic-local days `[from, to)`. Each event or visit is placed by the zone of its own doctor's clinic. `bucket_start` is clinic-local wall-clock time, not an instant, so with clinics in different zones the series merges the same local day (or hour) of every clinic.
Cancellations in [from, to) grouped by the reason text into transport, illness, travel, work, weather, felt_better, insurance and other. Counts only: no reason text.

The bookings, reschedules or cancellations (`kind`) made in the clinic-local days [from, to), by the day the change happened and not the day of the visit, newest first. `reason` (cancelled only) narrows to one cancellation-reason category, grouped as in `/cancellation-reasons`. `total` counts the whole range and filters, whatever `limit` (1 to 100, default 50) and `cursor` say. A viewer gets initials and no reason text.

The day's appointments as CSV (one row each: doctor, time, status, patient, phone, email, cancellation reason, timezone: the IANA zone the time column is in), for `date` (clinic-local) and optionally one doctor. Owner and admin get full details; a viewer gets initials and a masked phone and no email or reason. Cells that would run as a spreadsheet formula are neutralised.
Free 30-minute slots starting within the next `hours` (default 48), soonest first. Staff may book any of them, including inside the lead-time window.
Booked appointments by weekday (1 = Monday) and local start hour over [from, to), for the clinic or one doctor.

Utilisation, fill rate, cancellation rate, no-show rate, median booking lead time and reschedules over the clinic-local days [from, to), each with the previous period of the same length and the difference. A rate is null when its denominator is zero.

Each active doctor's day as a timeline with statuses booked, arrived, no_show and cancelled, the next free gap and a running-behind flag. `date` is a clinic-local day; without it, each doctor's clinic's today. Synthetic patients are left out. A viewer gets initials and a masked phone.

post.description: Give back one reserved email whose send failed, so a failure does not use the allowance.

Take one email from the day's and the month's allowance before sending it, atomically: under
any number of concurrent senders the caps are never exceeded. A refusal is a normal answer
(``granted`` false and the cap that said no), not an error: the caller just does not send.

parameters.description: `ack`: a booking acknowledgement, which may use the whole day. `other` (the default): any other email (reminders, staff emails, the doctor's arrival email); its day stops EMAIL_ACK_RESERVE short of EMAIL_DAILY_LIMIT, so the room kept for acknowledgements cannot be used up by them. The month has no reserve. It is optional, and defaults to `other`, so a caller that does not say (the patient app during a rollout, before it sends `ack`) is held back from the reserve rather than allowed to spend it: the safe direction.
